checkpoints.title: Foundation — path-tagged DOM + click-to-select top-level layer
checkpoints.goal: End-to-end tracer: every rendered scene element carries a `data-scene-path` attribute, and clicking the canvas sets `selectedPath` to the topmost top-level layer at that point. No drill-in, no drag, no chrome changes — the existing `is-canvas-selected` outline still applies. Establishes the click → selectedPath pipeline that later checkpoints extend.
checkpoints.testing_strategy: Manual: open http://localhost:3000/editor?scene=title. Click on the codecaine logo → hierarchy + inspector switch to that layer (existing `is-canvas-selected` outline appears). Click on bg-video → selects bg-video. Click on the same logo again → still selects the top-level logo (no drill yet). Inspect element: every rendered layer wrapper should carry `data-scene-path="<index>"` and nested children carry the `.children.<i>...` extension. Type check: `npm run build` passes.

task_groups.title: Renderer path tagging
task_groups.objective: Thread a `path` string through the imperative scene-renderer mount/update paths so every wrapper element ends up with `wrapper.dataset.scenePath` set. Top-level wrappers get `"0"`, `"1"`, …; nested children mounted via the regular `children` array get `"<parent>.children.<i>"`. Glyph-group sub-layers/foreign-media children are out of scope here — CP2 extends tagging into them. The path must remain accurate after reorders and re-renders, so set it on every code path that produces or reuses a wrapper (`mountObject`, `updateChildren`, `reorderChildren`).

Concretely: (1) Add a `path` parameter to `mountObject(parent, obj, beforeEl, path)` and set `wrapper.dataset.scenePath = path` immediately after the existing `wrapper.dataset.layerId = obj.id` block. (2) In the regular-children mount loop (current line ~190), pass `${path}.children.${i}` per child. (3) Add a `path` param to `updateChildren(parentEl, childArray, path)` and to `remountObject(parent, oldEl, obj, path)`. For each child, the per-child path is `${path}.children.${i}` (or just `${i}` when called from `renderScene` with parent path `""`). When a child is reused (the `applyObjectStyles(el, child, entry)` branch), still set `el.dataset.scenePath = childPath` so reorders update the path. (4) In the recursive `updateChildren(el, child.children)` call, pass `${childPath}` as the parent path argument. (5) In `renderScene`, the top-level for-loop calls `mountObject(root, obj, null, String(i))` and `updateChildren(root, scene.objects, '')` (parent path empty so children get `"0"`, `"1"`, …). (6) Update `reorderChildren(parentEl, childArray, parentPath)` to also re-stamp `dataset.scenePath` on each child as it walks `order`, so a reorder fixes paths even when no other mutation occurred. tasks.title: Generalize `pickScenePathAt` for deep hits + cmd-gated background filter
tasks.description: Update `apps/scene-engine/src/lib/hit-test.ts` (created in CP1). Change the signature from `pickScenePathAt(event, options?: { topLevelOnly?: boolean })` to `pickScenePathAt(event, options?: { cmd?: boolean; stageEl?: HTMLElement })`. Behavior: (1) `document.elementFromPoint(event.clientX, event.clientY)` then walk up via `closest('[data-scene-path]')` to get the deepest tagged element. Return `null` if none. (2) If `options.stageEl` is provided AND the resolved element is background-like (delegate to `isBackgroundLikeEl(el, stageEl)` from `./background-detect`), and `options.cmd` is NOT true, walk further up the ancestor chain looking for the next tagged ancestor that is NOT background-like; if none found, return `null` (the click hit only background, plain click should miss). (3) When `options.cmd` IS true, do not apply the background filter — the deepest tagged element wins (which is what the user wanted to grab the background). (4) Return the deepest non-filtered element's `dataset.scenePath` verbatim — no top-level slicing. Drop the old `topLevelOnly` parameter entirely; CP1's CanvasPanel call site is being rewritten in TG3 of this checkpoint, so no other callers exist. Hidden layers (`visible:false`) are not in the DOM (top-level skipped by `mountObject`) or have `display:none` (glyph-group sub-layers via `applyObjectStyles`) — `elementFromPoint` skips both, so no explicit filter is needed.

checkpoints.title: Drag-to-reposition with percentage write-back (two-tier rule)
checkpoints.goal: Mousedown-drag on a selected (or about-to-be-selected) layer rewrites `transform.x` / `transform.y` as percent numbers. Two-tier rule enforced: mousedown anywhere inside a `glyph-group` (including drilled-in children) drags the enclosing glyph-group; mousedown on a child of a generic `group` moves only that child within its parent. task_groups.objective: A React hook in `apps/scene-engine/app/editor/_components/canvas/useCanvasDrag.ts` that owns mousedown/mousemove/mouseup lifecycle on the stage. tasks.description: Create `apps/scene-engine/app/editor/_components/canvas/useCanvasDrag.ts` — first file under a new `canvas/` subdirectory. Export a default hook `useCanvasDrag({ stageRef }: { stageRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> }): { onMouseDown: (e: React.MouseEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => void; suppressNextClickRef: React.MutableRefObject<boolean> }`. Internals: (1) Read `scene` and `mutateObjectAt` from `useEditorStore` via individual selectors. (2) Two refs: `dragStateRef = useRef<{ targetPath: string; startTransform: TransformExplicit; startClientX: number; startClientY: number; rectWidth: number; rectHeight: number; moved: boolean } | null>(null)` and `suppressNextClickRef = useRef(false)`. (3) `MOVE_THRESHOLD = 3` (screen pixels) — until exceeded, treat as click not drag. (4) Define `onMouseDown(e)` wrapped in `useCallback`. Body: only handle left button (`e.button !== 0` → return). Resolve `hitPath = pickScenePathAt(e, { cmd: e.metaKey || e.ctrlKey, stageEl: stageRef.current ?? undefined })` from `@/lib/hit-test`. If `!hitPath || !scene` return. Resolve `target = resolveDragTarget(scene, hitPath)` from `@/lib/drag-target`. If `!target` return (e.g. fill-mode). Get `rect = stageRef.current.getBoundingClientRect()`. Initialize `dragStateRef.current = { targetPath: target.path, startTransform: target.object.transform as TransformExplicit, startClientX: e.clientX, startClientY: e.clientY, rectWidth: rect.width, rectHeight: rect.height, moved: false }`. Attach `window.addEventListener('mousemove', onWinMove)` and `window.addEventListener('mouseup', onWinUp, { once: true })`. (5) `onWinMove(ev: MouseEvent)`: if no `dragStateRef.current` return. Compute `dx = ev.clientX - state.startClientX`, `dy = ev.clientY - state.startClientY`. If not state.moved and `Math.hypot(dx, dy) < MOVE_THRESHOLD` return (still a click). Set `state.moved = true`. Compute `next = applyDragDelta(state.startTransform, dx, dy, state.rectWidth, state.rectHeight)`. Call `mutateObjectAt(state.targetPath, { transform: { x: next.x, y: next.y } })`. (6) `onWinUp()`: detach mousemove. If `dragStateRef.current?.moved` set `suppressNextClickRef.current = true`. Clear `dragStateRef.current = null`. Note: mousemove + mouseup are stable functions defined via `useRef` containers OR via `useCallback` with stable deps; simplest is to define them inside `onMouseDown` so they close over the live state — that's fine because they detach themselves on mouseup. (7) `useEffect` cleanup: on hook unmount, if `dragStateRef.current` is set, remove any lingering window listeners (defensive — store the move/up handlers on the ref so cleanup can call removeEventListener with the same references). Return `{ onMouseDown, suppressNextClickRef }`. tasks.description: Create `apps/scene-engine/src/lib/resize-math.ts`. Export types `HandleId = 'nw' | 'n' | 'ne' | 'e' | 'se' | 's' | 'sw' | 'w'`, `ResizeStart = { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; anchorOffsetX: number; anchorOffsetY: number }`, and `ResizeResult = { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }`. Implementation: (1) Compute start bbox edges from the start state: `left = start.x - start.width * start.anchorOffsetX`, `top = start.y - start.height * start.anchorOffsetY`, `right = left + start.width`, `bottom = top + start.height`. (2) Classify the handle: `movesWest = handle in {nw,sw,w}`, `movesEast = handle in {ne,se,e}`, `movesNorth = handle in {nw,ne,n}`, `movesSouth = handle in {sw,se,s}`. (3) Apply delta to dragged edges: `left += movesWest ? delta.dxPct : 0`; same for right/east, top/north, bottom/south. (4) Aspect lock — corners only (`(movesWest||movesEast) && (movesNorth||movesSouth)`): if `options?.aspectLock`, compute `aspect = start.width / Math.max(start.height, MIN_SIZE)` and current `w = right-left`, `h = bottom-top`; if `Math.abs(w - start.width) >= Math.abs((h - start.height) * aspect)`, conform height (`h = w / aspect`; if movesNorth `top = bottom - h` else `bottom = top + h`); else conform width (`w = h * aspect`; if movesWest `left = right - w` else `right = left + w`). (5) Min-size clamp: if `right - left < MIN_SIZE`, push the moving edge back so the gap is exactly `MIN_SIZE` (movesWest → `left = right - MIN_SIZE`; movesEast → `right = left + MIN_SIZE`); same for top/bottom. (6) Recompute (x, y) from the new bbox plus the start anchor offsets: `newWidth = right - left`, `newHeight = bottom - top`, `newX = left + newWidth * start.anchorOffsetX`, `newY = top + newHeight * start.anchorOffsetY`. (7) Return all four rounded via `Number(v.toFixed(2))`. JSDoc: explain stage-percent coordinate space; anchorOffset 0/0.5/1 maps to left/center/right (or top/center/bottom); v1 ignores rotation/scale (axis-aligned only); aspect lock applies to corners only.

tasks.description: Create `apps/scene-engine/app/editor/_components/canvas/useCanvasKeyboardNudge.ts`. Default-export `useCanvasKeyboardNudge(): void` (no inputs, no return — purely an effect). Internals: (1) Read three store slots: `const scene = useEditorStore(s => s.scene)`, `const selectedPath = useEditorStore(s => s.selectedPath)`, `const mutateObjectAt = useEditorStore(s => s.mutateObjectAt)`. (2) Constants: `const STEP = 1`, `const SHIFT_STEP = 5` (percent — the spec's 'TBD step size' resolved by the testing strategy as 'shift = 5%'). (3) Helper `function isEditableTarget(t: EventTarget | null): boolean` — true if `t instanceof HTMLElement` AND (`t.tagName === 'INPUT' || t.tagName === 'TEXTAREA' || t.tagName === 'SELECT' || t.isContentEditable`). Used to bail out so typing into the inspector doesn't nudge the selected layer. (4) Inside a `useEffect(() => { ... return () => window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey) }, [scene, selectedPath, mutateObjectAt])` block, define `function onKey(e: KeyboardEvent)`: bail if `!scene || !selectedPath`; bail if `isEditableTarget(e.target)`; `let dx = 0, dy = 0`; switch `e.key`: `'ArrowLeft'` → `dx = -1`; `'ArrowRight'` → `dx = 1`; `'ArrowUp'` → `dy = -1`; `'ArrowDown'` → `dy = 1`; default → return (do not consume non-arrow keys). Resolve target: `const target = resolveObject(scene, selectedPath) as SceneObject | null`; if `!target` return. Cast `transform = target.transform`; if `(transform as { mode?: string }).mode === 'fill'` return (fill-mode layers have no x/y to nudge). `e.preventDefault()` (consumed — stops page scroll). Apply step: `const step = e.shiftKey ? SHIFT_STEP : STEP`; cast `t = transform as TransformExplicit`; resolve numeric current values mirroring useCanvasResize: `const curX = typeof t.x === 'number' ? t.x : (NAMED_X[t.x] ?? 0)`; same for `curY` against `NAMED_Y`; compute `nextX = Number((curX + dx * step).toFixed(2))` (only if dx !== 0); same for `nextY`. Build the patch: only include the axis that actually moved so an untouched named pin (e.g. `"center"`) is preserved — `const patch: { x?: number; y?: number } = {}; if (dx !== 0) patch.x = nextX; if (dy !== 0) patch.y = nextY`. Call `mutateObjectAt(selectedPath, { transform: patch })`. (5) Attach inside the effect: `window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)`. The whole hook is scene/selection-dependent — re-running the effect on selection change is cheap (one listener swap) and ensures `onKey` always closes over the freshest store snapshot.
